summary: Documentation only, two files, no code, no test, no CHANGELOG. (1) docs/kubernetes.md, the paragraph opening 'That check is `python3`, which the image carries, because': make its first reason historical ('the role container had no client for any of these servers when it was written'), keep the other two reasons and the 'What it proves…' sentence word for word, and add one sentence saying the first reason is the one that changed: the image this repository builds carries psql, redis-cli, sqlite3, nc and dig from dispatch://INFRA-221's merge on 2026-10-25 onward, a role has them once its deployment pins a digest built from that merge or a later main commit, a role on an older digest has none, and python3 runs on both. (2) AGENTS.md 'Run a database, broker or server the work needs' row: replace its last sentence 'A tool that works on the checkout belongs on the issue's own disk instead' with 'The other half of the question is the *Get a tool a role's work needs into the pod* row: a service the work talks to runs in the cluster, a tool works on the issue's checkout'. The recommended wording, the proof commands and the acceptance check script are in the plan document.
baseline: Step 0: jj git fetch and find both clauses on main@origin by their text, not by line number; check whether PR #2182 (dispatch://INFRA-234) has merged. Plan read main at 6ede52ccb376.
tasks: Task 1: rewrite the reason paragraph in docs/kubernetes.md as above, wrapped at 100 columns; the ([Worker image](#worker-image)) link stays; the python3 example is not rewritten (dispatch://INFRA-215 holds that).

Task 2: replace the last sentence of the AGENTS.md 'Run a database' row with the mirror pointer; the rest of the row is main's as of when you start (with #2182's middle sentence if it merged); the tool row does not change.

Task 3: prove the image claim on the main-built worker image of 6ede52ccb376 or a later main commit: go run github.com/google/go-containerregistry/cmd/crane@v0.20.6 digest/config/export on ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-<12 hex>, revision label names a main commit, tar -tvf lists usr/bin/psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig python3, and the release run's worker-image build log shows the Dockerfile check step's version output. Negative control: ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-92dbeea3d391 lists none of the five; a role container on the deployment's current digest has none (command -v). All downloads under $TMPDIR. If no main image exists yet, do not wait: use INFRA-221's PR head image sha-98e5f6a8c72c plus the Dockerfile diff 98e5f6a8..6ede52cc (one comment), say so in the E2E line, tell the architect.

Task 4: run the throwaway check /legion/scratch/tmp/infra372/check_clauses.py (full text in the plan document's appendix; not committed) from the workspace: it compares both files with the merge base of main@origin and @ and allows only the two edits; it must print OK and exit 0. Also run .github/scripts/check-private-names.sh and check-plugin-names.sh.
One commit with docs/kubernetes.md and AGENTS.md, push, open the PR with 'Dispatch: INFRA-372' and the E2E lines per skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md.
integration: PR #2182 (dispatch://INFRA-234) edits the middle sentence of the same AGENTS.md row (line 128 at 6ede52cc); this issue edits its last sentence. Whichever merges second conflicts on that one line; the resolution keeps both changes. In docs/kubernetes.md #2182's nearest change is two unchanged lines above the reason paragraph and its next is two paragraphs below, so no conflict is expected there. On a real conflict only: forward merge of main (skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md), never a rebase, then re-run Task 4.

implement: legion-worker: its pr-body reference for the PR body and the E2E line, default-branch-check before the push, conflicts-and-rewrites for the forward merge if #2182 lands first and the AGENTS.md row conflicts

findings.finding: Three adjacent sentences of the workload section are also left incomplete by the merge or older ('Speaking the protocol is a client library onto the issue's own disk…', 'those arrive through the image's package runners…', 'Its own pod cannot hold one'), and INFRA-215 did not bank them.
findings.answer: Sent to the architect over Envoy; the architect kept INFRA-372 at its two clauses and banked all three on dispatch://INFRA-215 (v10). The plan records them as out of scope with that disposition.

findings.finding: Under 'because', listing the clients the image now carries would reverse the sentence's justification; the plan must say whether python3 has a current reason.
findings.answer: The first reason becomes historical ('had … when it was written'); the added sentence states the measured present fact that python3 is on both the old and the new digest, without claiming python3 is preferred.

findings.finding: 'Checked against the merged text' needs a named baseline and a rule for keeping #2182's edits when both land.
findings.answer: Step 0 reads main@origin at start; the check compares against the merge base of main@origin and the head, and takes the row's middle sentence from that base, so #2182's sentence survives; the integration section gives the conflict resolution.

findings.finding: 'What the image actually carries' needs a named artifact and proof strength while the main-built image may not be published.
findings.answer: Task 3 requires the main-built image by digest with its revision label, a filesystem listing and the build log's version lines; the fallback (PR head image plus the Dockerfile diff) is stated, recorded in the E2E line, and reported to the architect; no rollout is claimed.

findings.finding: The preservation and two-way pointer requirements had no deciding comparison.
findings.answer: check_clauses.py: byte comparison against the merge base allowing only the two replacements, whitespace-normalised word-for-word checks on the surviving reasons, required facts in the new sentence, and both pointers; run by the planner against the recommended edits (OK) and five broken copies (each refused).
